# Findings (auto-generated by `src/analysis.py`)

Periods: before = 2026-06-08..2026-07-05 (n=28,915), incident = 2026-07-06..2026-07-19 (n=16,189).

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| D7 retention before | 29.8% |
| D7 retention incident weeks | 22.8% |
| change | -7.0 pp (95% CI -7.8 … -6.1, p=2.3e-57) |

## Decomposition of the change

| driver | contribution | share of drop |
|---|---|---|
| Android 4.2.0 onboarding bug (rate) | -2.8 pp | 41% |
| Channel mix: influencer campaign | -3.8 pp | 55% |
| Other (seasonality / noise) | -0.3 pp | 5% |
| **Total** | **-7.0 pp** | 100% |

Influencer share of signups: 1.1% → 25.6%; its D7 retention ≈ 13.5%
vs 26.3% for other channels in the same weeks.

## Android 4.2.0 vs other Android versions (incident weeks)

| metric | 4.2.0 | other Android | diff (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|---|
| signup → address | 51.3% | 85.9% | -34.7 pp (-36.8 … -32.5) |
| D7 retention | 18.7% | 26.0% | -7.3 pp (-9.8 … -4.8) |

Later funnel steps (address → payment → order) are unchanged, so the loss is isolated to one screen.
